Hello,

I desployed already my application, but it crashes as I click on the Load-Threat-Map-Button Here is the link to the app: https://marinemammals-threatmaps.shinyapps.io/Test2/
If I upload the same app without the shapefiles everything works fine: Here is the link to this app: https://marinemammals-threatmaps.shinyapps.io/test1112/

It would be great If someone could help me out :)!

dat <- read.xlsx2("mmtb.xlsx", sheetName="Marine_mammal_Threat_database")

load("ras_two_sp.RData")

#exchange wrong level names
dat[which(dat$Longhurst_code == "Ausw"),"Longhurst_code"] <- "AUSW"

dat[which(dat$Longhurst_code == "Natr"),"Longhurst_code"] <- "NATR"
dat$Longhurst_code <- droplevels(dat$Longhurst_code)

#create lists for input
Fissi <- as.character(levels(droplevels(dat[which(dat$Taxa_group=="Fissipedia"),"Scientific_name"])))
Mysti <- as.character(levels(droplevels(dat[which(dat$Taxa_group=="Mysticeti"),"Scientific_name"])))
Pinni <- as.character(levels(droplevels(dat[which(dat$Taxa_group=="Pinnipedia"),"Scientific_name"])))
Siren <- as.character(levels(droplevels(dat[which(dat$Taxa_group=="Sirenia"),"Scientific_name"])))
Odonto <-  as.character(levels(droplevels(dat[which(dat$Taxa_group=="Odontoceti"),"Scientific_name"])))

fun_list_spec <- function(spec,spec_c ="default"){
  list_ <- list()

  for (i in 1:length(spec)) {
    if (spec_c == c("Fissipedia")){
      split_ <- strsplit(spec[i]," ")[[1]]
      ID_ <- paste0(substr(split_[1], 1, 3),substr(split_[2],1,2))
    } else {
      split_ <- strsplit(spec[i]," ")[[1]]
      ID_ <- paste0(substr(split_[1], 1, 2),substr(split_[2],1,3))
    }
    list_[[spec[i]]] <- ID_
  }
  return(list_)
}

li_fissi <- fun_list_spec(Fissi, "Fissipedia")
li_odonto <- fun_list_spec(Odonto)
li_mysti <- fun_list_spec(Mysti)
li_pinni <- fun_list_spec(Pinni)
li_siren <- fun_list_spec(Siren)

                                  ) #absolutePanel
                            ) #div
                   ) #interactive map

                   ,navbarMenu(title = "Data Explorer",
                               tabPanel(title = "Data Sources",

                                        fluidRow(column(7, offset = 1,
                                                        tags$h3("Database"),
                                                        "For the presented threat maps of marine mammals we use a database produced by",
                                                        tags$em(tags$a(href="http://www.biom.uni-freiburg.de/MarineMammalThreatDatabase", "Isabel C. Avila from the Albert-Ludwig University of Freiburg, Germany.")),
                                                        "This database systematically reviewed, categorized and geo-referenced information from
                                                        more than 1700 publications about threats affecting 121 marine mammal species worldwide between 1991 and 2016."),
                                                 column(3, offset = 1, tags$a(href = "http://www.biom.uni-freiburg.de/MarineMammalThreatDatabase",
                                                                              tags$img( width = 100, src = "Uni_Logo.png"))
                                                 )),

                                        hr(),

                                        fluidRow(column(7, offset = 1,
                                                        tags$h3("Species Distribution"),
                                                        "We use the predicted marine mammal species distributions produced by",
                                                        tags$em(tags$a(href = "http://aquamaps.org/", "Aquamaps, ")),
                                                        "which is an online atlas of species distributions."),
                                                 column(3, offset = 1, tags$a(href = "http://aquamaps.org/", tags$img(height = 100, width = 100,
                                                                                                                      src = "aquamaps.jpg"))
                                                 )),

                                        hr(),

                                        fluidRow(column(7, offset = 1,
                                                        tags$h3("Exclusive Economic Zones"),
                                                        "The countries' national waters were defined with the boundary definitions for 195 countries
                                                        with territorial seas. These zones are called Exlcusive Economic Zones (EEZ).",
                                                        tags$p(tags$em("VLIZ (2014), Union of ESRI Country shapefile and Exclusive Economic Zones, available online at",

  ###########################
  # server.R
  ###########################

  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({
      leaflet(options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 1, maxZoom = 18)) %>%
        setView(lng = 10, lat = 0, zoom = 2) %>%
        addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap") %>%
        addPolygons(data=Longhurst,
                    color = "red",
                    fillOpacity = 0,
                    group = "Longhurst Provinces",
                    weight=1,
                    smoothFactor = 0.5,
                    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(color = "white", weight = 2,bringToFront = TRUE),
                    label = Longhurst$ProvDescr,
                    labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, textOnly = TRUE, opacity = 1, textsize='15px')

        ) %>%
        addPolygons(data=EEZ_land,
                    color = "#444444",
                    fillOpacity = 0,
                    group = "Exclusive Economic Zones",
                    weight=1,
                    smoothFactor = 0.5,
                    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(color = "white", weight = 2,bringToFront = TRUE),
                    label = EEZ_land$Country,
                    labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, textOnly = TRUE, opacity = 1, textsize='15px')
        ) %>%
        addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("Longhurst Provinces",
                                           "Exclusive Economic Zones"
                                           ),
                         position = "topleft",
                         options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = F)
        ) %>%
        hideGroup("Longhurst Provinces") %>%
        hideGroup("Exclusive Economic Zones")

    })

    ##################
    #options:
    ##################

    observe({

      #Species Uptade
      y <- input$taxa

      # Can use character(0) to remove all choices
      # if (is.null(y))
      #  y <- character(0)

      if (y=="Fissipedia")
        updateSelectInput(session, "species",
                          choices = li_fissi,
                          selected = tail(y, 1)
        )
      if (y=="Mysticeti")
        updateSelectInput(session, "species",
                          choices = li_mysti,
                          selected = tail(y, 1)
        )
      if (y=="Odontoceti")
        updateSelectInput(session, "species",
                          choices = li_odonto,
                          selected = tail(y, 1)
        )
      if (y=="Pinnipedia")
        updateSelectInput(session, "species",
                          choices = li_pinni,
                          selected = tail(y, 1)
        )
      if (y=="Sirenia")
        updateSelectInput(session, "species",
                          choices = li_siren,
                          selected = tail(y, 1)
        )
    })

    observe({
      #Threat attribute Uptade:
      x <- input$threat

      # Can use character(0) to remove all choices
      #  if (is.null(x))
      #    x <- character(0)

      if (x=='sum')
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = c("All" = "sum"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1))

      if (x=="BYCA")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "BYCA", "By-catch" = "BYCA_1", "Shield-net" = "BYCA_2", "Ghost-net" = "BYCA_3", "Other interaction" = "BYCA_4"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )

      if (x=="DHAR")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = c("All" = "DHAR", "Commercial" = "DHAR_1", "Subsistence" = "DHAR_2", "Control" = "DHAR_3", "Research" = "DHAR_4", "Alive Capture" = "DHAR_5"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )

      if (x=="POLL")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "POLL", "Liquid wastes" = "POLL_1", "Solid wastes" = "POLL_2", "Noise" = "POLL_3", "Radioactive" = "POLL_4", "Thermal" = "POLL_5"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )

      if (x=="TRAF")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "TRAF", "Boat without collision" = "TRAF_1", "Boat with collision" = "TRAF_2", "People" = "TRAF_3", "Aircraft" = "TRAF_4"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )

      if (x=="INFE")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "INFE", "Infections" = "INFE_1", "Algea bloom" = "INFE_2", "Introduced Species" = "INFE_3"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1))

      if (x=="HABI")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "HABI", "Food limitation" = "HABI_1", "Habitat Removal" = "HABI_2"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )

      if (x=="OCEA")
        updateSelectInput(session, "attribute",
                          choices = list("All" = "OCEA", "Storms" = "OCEA_1", "Temperature" = "OCEA_2", "ENSO" = "OCEA_3", "Ice cover" = "OCEA_4", "Geomagnetic field" = "OCEA_5"),
                          selected = tail(x, 1)
        )
    })

    #################
    #load threat map:
    #################

    observeEvent(input$Load, {
      output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({
        leaflet(options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 1, maxZoom = 18)) %>%
          setView(lng = 10, lat = 0, zoom = 2) %>%
          addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap") %>%
          ##add the selected rasterfile:
          addRasterImage(ras_two_sp[[paste0(isolate(input$species),"_",isolate(input$attribute))]],
                         colors = colorFactor(c("grey", "orange", "darkred"),
                                              values(ras_two_sp[[paste0(isolate(input$species),"_",isolate(input$attribute))]]),
                                              na.color = "transparent"),
                         opacity=0.6) %>%
          addLegend("topleft",
                    pal = colorFactor(c("grey", "orange", "darkred"),
                                      values(ras_two_sp[[paste0(isolate(input$species),"_",isolate(input$attribute))]]),
                                      na.color = "transparent"),
                    values = values(ras_two_sp[[paste0(isolate(input$species),"_",isolate(input$attribute))]]),
                    title = "Reported Threats") %>%
          addPolygons(data=Longhurst,
                      color = "red",
                      fillOpacity = 0,
                      group = "Longhurst Provinces",
                      weight=1,
                      smoothFactor = 0.5,
                      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(color = "white", weight = 2,bringToFront = TRUE),
                      label = Longhurst$ProvDescr,
                      labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, textOnly = TRUE, opacity = 1, textsize='15px')

          ) %>%
          addPolygons(data=EEZ_land,
                      color = "#444444",
                      fillOpacity = 0,
                      group = "Exclusive Economic Zones",
                      weight=1,
                      smoothFactor = 0.5,
                      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(color = "white", weight = 2,bringToFront = TRUE),
                      label = EEZ_land$Country,
                      labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, textOnly = TRUE, opacity = 1, textsize='15px')
          ) %>%
          addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("Longhurst Provinces",
                                             "Exclusive Economic Zones"
                                             ),
                           position = "topleft",
                           options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = F)
          ) %>%
           hideGroup("Longhurst Provinces") %>%
           hideGroup("Exclusive Economic Zones") #%>%
         # hideGroup("Ocean Basins")

      }) #renderLeaflet
    })
  }

  shinyApp(ui, server)

I'd like this app to be accessible online, and I'm aware that hosting Shiny apps is restricted to some operating systems like Ubuntu.  Is it possible/has anyone succeeded in hosting a Shiny app that calls an external Windows application?

My experience outside of Windows is non-existent, so I may be a little slow on the uptake.  Apologies in advance!

Howard

get_logs <- function(id, entries){
    accountDetails <- accountInfo("...")
    client <- lucidClient(shinyappsServerInfo()$url, accountDetails)
    logs <- client$getLogs( id, entries, FALSE, NULL)
    nn <- gregexpr("\n", logs, fixed = T)
    length(nn[[1]])
    nn <- as.numeric(nn[[1]][1:length(nn[[1]])])
    data_logs <- data.frame(from = c(0, nn))
    data_logs$to <- c(nn, nchar(logs))
    data_logs$log <- ""
    data_logs$from <- data_logs$from + 1
    data_logs$to <- data_logs$to - 1
    data_logs$log <- apply(data_logs, 1, function(x) substr(logs, x[1], x[2]))
    return(data_logs)
}

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Can I not use shinyapps.io from a Windows OS? Or is it only the libraries that would have to be linux compatible? I am new to this.
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Can I not use shinyapps.io from a Windows OS? Or is it only the libraries that would have to be linux compatible? I am new to this.
messages.body_plain:
Ravi,

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> runs on Linux, which means the code you write and the packages you use must be compatible with Linux. Most, but not all R packages are. This also means you can not use any Windows specific calls or utilities.

That said, this does NOT mean you can't develop your application on Windows, and then deploy it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. It simply means the code must be written in a compatible cross platform.

Hope that helps,
-Andy

messages.subject: No graphs displaid in deployed Shiny app
messages.subject_clean: No graphs displaid in deployed Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

first message in this mailing list, yeah (?) !

So, i'm building an app with Shiny. The basic idea is to perform PCA Analysis with FactomineR on data that the user can upload (excel sheet), and then to display the results in several graphs :

p<-res.hcpc<-HCPC(res ,nb.clust=-1,consol=FALSE,min=3,max=10,graph=TRUE)
    plot(p, choice = "2D.map")

On local, everything works well, I can upload the data and display the graphs correctly. The problem comes when I deploy the app. No error :

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
[...]
Application successfully deployed

But when I try to do exactly the same thing on the web, no graphs are shown (but everything else seems to be working fine).

Any idea where that could come from ?

Cheers,

Léolo

messages.subject: computationally intensive app runs on laptop in 2 mins but takes 20 mins on Virtual machine
messages.subject_clean: computationally intensive app runs on laptop in 2 mins but takes 20 mins on Virtual machine
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I have developed a computationally intensive shiny app. The process runs on my local laptop ( 32 GB RAN, core i-7 2.90 GHx, 4 core, 8 processors, 1 TB SSD) in about 2 mins but the same process takes about 20 minutes when hosted as a virtualized server instance from the CentOS Virtual Machine in my universities DMZ network ( 32 GB total memory, x86_64, 8 CPUs, 1 thread per core, 4 cores per socket, 2 sockets with one web process per shiny application).

I am trying to understand what could cause the huge discrepancy in the processing time on the two machines.

Any help in this regard is greatly appreciated.

Regards,
M
